title: Hilbert's tenth problem undecidability via full MRDP
statement: There exist a finite number of variables and an integer multivariate polynomial whose solvability predicate, with one input parameter and existential natural-number witnesses, is not computable; an integer-witness version should follow by four-square substitution.

source.citation: D. Larchey-Wendling and Y. Forster, Hilbert's Tenth Problem in Coq (FSCD 2019); Aristotle completion email received 2026-08-11

criteria: complete Aristotle source bundle imported into the pinned repository toolchain
lake build succeeds with no sorry, admit, native_decide, or added axioms
#print axioms is contained in propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
audit the halting-set reduction, bounded-universal closure, MRDP normalization, MvPolynomial evaluation, and natural-to-integer four-square step for circularity and type-faithful semantics

notes: Aristotle reports a full Lean MRDP/H10 chain, but only the email summary is available here. A full Coq mechanization already exists, so this is not a first formalization in any prover; it may be a first complete Lean formalization. Do not promote to PROVED until source and independent verifier artifacts land.
